newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan expenses boosted by investments.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan expenses boosted by investments.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc chairman and chief executive Douglas Warner III said Wednesday the firm's investments in certain businesses with big potential caused expenses to grow at a faster rate than revenue in the first quarter of 1997.

"We are investing in areas that we think have enormous potential," he told reporters after the annual shareholders meeting. He it would be a "bad thing" if expense growth continued to outpace revenue growth over the long term.
Warner said the company also aimes to make its expenses in its cyclical businesses variable.
In the first quarter of 1997 J.P. Morgan's expenses rose 9.8 percent over the prior-year period while revenue was up 5.3 percent.

Warner identified the areas with big potential as the equities business, emerging markets, investment management and private banking. "Those are all long-term kinds of things," he said, adding that "being a leader in the equities business is our goal."
"If you have revenue trends in a quarter (lagging expenses)...that doesn't influence my thinking with respect to those investments," Warner said.
Warner said, "We have worked hard ... and it is an important goal, to have expenses in a number of the cyclical businesses variable through cycles."

He cited the formation of the Pinnacle Alliance to manage one-third of the company's technology infrastructure. Partners in the alliance are Computer Sciences Corp, Andersen Consulting, AT&T Solutions, a unit of AT&T Corp, and Bell Atlantic Corp's Bell Atlantic Network Integration.
He said one objective of the alliance is that if volumes contract because of cyclicality, "someone else in effect uses their big capacity to absorb the cost."

In his report to shareholders, Warner noted the consolidation that has swept through the financial services industry. "Clearly, we understand that changes in the competitive landscape present both opportunities and challenges, and we explore all of our options actively," he said, adding, "The company has a strong position today and none of the recent business combinations changes that."
After the meeting he told a questioner that in the past J.P. Morgan has found it better to build businesses than buy them.
Asked by a shareholder if a stock split was possible, he said it is not being considered at the moment.
